name: SOUTH AFRICA

flag.title: South Africa
flag.note: Six colours, Y-shape, unique in the world

lead: South Africa sits at the very tip of Africa, where the Atlantic and Indian oceans nearly meet. It holds snowy mountains, scorching deserts, wild savannahs, and whale-watched coastlines all in one country. Eleven official languages make it the world's most multilingual nation — and its rainbow flag tells the whole story.

facts.label: Land area
facts.sub: roughly twice the size of France

sections.geography: A land of two oceans & peaks

geo: South Africa wraps around the southern tip of Africa. The flat Karoo desert stretches across the centre, while the dramatic Drakensberg mountains form a giant wall along the east.
Two oceans frame the coastline — the cold Atlantic in the west and the warm Indian Ocean in the east. They meet near Cape Agulhas, the true southern tip of the continent.
animals: South Africa is home to the Big Five — lion, leopard, elephant, rhino, and buffalo — all easily spotted in Kruger National Park, one of Africa's largest game reserves.
The waters off Hermanus are the world's best place to watch southern right whales from shore. Penguins waddle on Boulders Beach, just 40 km from Cape Town.
culture: South Africa has 11 official languages — more than any other country. Greetings change every few kilometres: 'Sawubona' in Zulu, 'Molo' in Xhosa, 'Hallo' in Afrikaans.
Braai (barbecue) is the great national pastime — families gather around charcoal fires every weekend. Rugby is almost a religion, and the Springboks are World Cup champions.
history: For millennia, San hunter-gatherers and Bantu-speaking farmers called southern Africa home. Dutch settlers arrived in 1652, followed by the British, reshaping the land through conflict.
Apartheid — a cruel system of racial separation — ruled from 1948 until 1994. Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison before becoming the country's first democratically elected president.
wows: South Africa is the only country to have voluntarily dismantled its own nuclear weapons.
Johannesburg sits atop the world's largest gold reef — more gold mined here than anywhere on Earth.
SA has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town, and Bloemfontein.
Boulders Beach hosts over 3,000 wild African penguins just 40 km from Cape Town.
South Africa produces around 80% of the world's platinum supply.
Baobab trees in Limpopo can live 2,000 years, storing thousands of litres inside.
Table Mountain is ~600 million years old — far older than the Himalayas.

myths.fact: Most of SA is dry grassland (veld) and semi-desert Karoo — true rainforest covers only a tiny sliver of the south coast.
Wild lions live only in protected reserves like Kruger — city residents are far more likely to spot a hadeda ibis in the garden.
